<USER_REQUEST>
 this is project repo : https://github.com/Jahid-Tamboli/NagrikOne.git , so analyze it properly and deeply and  extractt the files/data  and update my nagrikone project proeprly and carefully # NagrikOne — Premium Authentication Redesign + Aesthetic 3D Animations

Act as a **senior full-stack developer, UI/UX designer, and motion-design specialist**. Work directly on my existing NagrikOne project and improve the current website. Do not create a separate demo website or rebuild the entire project from scratch.

## 1. Current Priority: Simplify Authentication

For now, we are temporarily removing SMS OTP and email OTP authentication. We will implement OTP later.

### Sign Up page
Create a beautiful, premium account-creation experience with:
- Full name
- Email address
- Mobile number as a profile/contact field only (no OTP verification)
- Password
- Confirm password
- Show/hide password control
- Terms and Privacy Policy checkbox
- Create Account button
- A link for existing users to Log In

### Login page
Create a matching Login page with:
- Email address or username
- Password
- Show/hide password control
- Remember me, if supported securely by the existing authentication architecture
- Forgot Password link only if a functional recovery flow exists; otherwise, provide a clear placeholder message rather than a fake working feature
- Login button
- A link for new users to Sign Up

### Authentication requirements
- Remove the SMS OTP tab, OTP input, Send OTP button, gateway configuration error, and unnecessary OTP-related UI from the user-facing authentication flow.
- Do not delete the existing OTP backend permanently. Keep reusable code where safe so OTP can be reintroduced later.
- Use the existing database, user model, session system, and authentication APIs wherever possible.
- If password authentication is not already implemented, implement it properly using secure password hashing and server-side validation.
- Never store plain-text passwords or hardcode cred
<truncated 4574 bytes>
em through client-side code.

## 6. Implementation and Testing Workflow

Follow this order:

1. Inspect the current codebase and identify all existing authentication components, routes, and session logic.
2. Explain the current authentication approach briefly and identify what must change to support password-based Sign Up and Login.
3. Implement secure registration and login.
4. Remove OTP from the active authentication UI without unnecessarily deleting reusable backend code.
5. Design and implement the new premium authentication pages.
6. Add the 3D visuals, animations, transitions, and responsive behavior.
7. Integrate the new UI with real backend authentication.
8. Test registration, duplicate-account errors, login success, incorrect passwords, session persistence, logout, protected routes, and mobile responsiveness.
9. Run the available lint, TypeScript, and build checks. Fix errors introduced by your changes.
10. Review the finished pages for accessibility, performance, readability, and visual consistency.

## 7. Final Report Required

When finished, report:
- Files changed.
- Authentication features actually implemented.
- Animation and UI improvements completed.
- Commands to run the project locally.
- Tests and build checks that passed or failed.
- Any remaining setup required.

**Important:** Do not stop after creating a design mockup. Implement the actual working pages, connect them to the existing backend, and verify the functionality. If a necessary authentication or database feature is missing, explain the issue and implement it safely rather than pretending it already works.
</USER_REQUEST>
